Session index transport record only; reviewed for session identity and serial control confirmation.
Single serial actor probed behavior, created fixtures, wrote Rust crypto and ZIP modules plus Cargo.toml, then was cancelled before finishing a buildable main.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the task as a clean-room clone of zip-password-finder with CLI parsing, dictionary attack, brute-force generation, ZIP handling, AES/ZipCrypto behavior, output formatting, and no source lookup or binary inspection.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first probed basics, then delegated five research areas to separate children and later assigned the entire implementation to one coder child rather than keeping implementation in the parent.
parallel.implementation: The five children produced markdown exploration reports, but the implementation child only began reading reports and probing; no Rust or other buildable reimplementation was returned before cancellation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The submitted parallel artifact contained exploration reports, assets, README, LICENSE, git metadata, and the original executable, not a new source tree or buildable implementation.
parallel.verification: Exploration children verified many behavioral details against the original, but there was no final integrated build or differential test of a produced clone.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The implementation scope was left unfinished after the implementation child was stopped, causing an artifact without a compilable solution and official compile_failed.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room reverse-engineering obligations and probed CLI parsing, ZIP encryption, AES and ZipCrypto, dictionary behavior, charset ordering, and output formats directly.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor kept responsibility for probing and implementation, tracked a local implementation plan, and then moved into writing a Rust project.
serial.implementation: The serial run created Cargo.toml and wrote core Rust modules including sha1, crc32, zipcrypto, inflate, and zipfile, but did not complete the entry point or the full executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact includes partial Rust source modules and Cargo.toml, but lacks the complete final assembly needed for the official build.
serial.verification: The serial actor ran many original-binary probes and some fixture experiments, but it did not reach an integrated verification cycle for its own implementation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run was cancelled before completing main.rs, CLI glue, build/install behavior, and final differential checks, so official evaluation also failed at compile_failed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required clean-room clone and split behavioral discovery into CLI, dictionary, brute force, ZIP handling, and output formatting reports.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same clean-room task and performed direct behavioral probing before implementing modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement understanding was broadly similar; the material difference was not task recognition but whether implementation work was recovered after interruption.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed discovery across five children, then made one late child responsible for the whole implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept probing and implementation under the main actor, using a local todo plan rather than child delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel separated research from implementation and depended on a late child handoff; serial owned the coding path directly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel transferred exploration through report files and a coder prompt; the reports were available, but the implementer did not finish consuming them into code.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial accumulated context locally through probes and carried it directly into module writing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an explicit report-to-child context boundary, while serial had no handoff boundary for its discovered requirements.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced no new implementation before artifact collection; implementation was delegated and then stopped.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a partial Rust implementation with crypto, ZIP, and inflate modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial made concrete source progress; parallel ended with reports only because the implementation child failed before returning code.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The implementation child was launched, then the active turn was cancelled and the child result reported failure before any implementation return.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle; its single main actor was cancelled while still implementing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a failed child-result boundary with no recovery; serial's incomplete state came from the main actor's own timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel exploration children shared workspace state and todo state, but final artifact inspection shows reports/assets rather than integrated source.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote source modules into one Rust project tree and the artifact captured those partial files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had no integrated implementation tree to build; serial had partial integrated modules but still lacked final assembly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified behavior during exploration but never verified a produced clone; official evaluation failed before tests ran.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified original behavior and fixtures but did not run an integrated build or official-aligned test of its partial clone; official evaluation failed before tests ran.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both lacked final acceptance evidence; parallel had no clone to test, while serial had unassembled partial source.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent substantial budget on exploration, launched implementation late, then closure occurred immediately after the implementation child was stopped.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used the full budget probing and writing modules, then was cancelled before finishing the executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both timed out, but parallel's closure passed through a failed child with no takeover, whereas serial's closure interrupted its own ongoing implementation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official outcome is not discordant: both completed evaluation and both failed at compile_failed with zero of 792 tests passed. The parallel run nevertheless differs because it left implementation inside a stopped child and submitted no new buildable source, while the serial run wrote partial Rust modules but was cancelled before completing final assembly.
parallel_contributors: A late implementation child was stopped before returning source and the parent did not recover the unfinished implementation scope.
The submitted parallel artifact contained exploration reports and assets rather than a compilable reimplementation.
serial_contributors: The serial actor made concrete source progress by writing Cargo.toml and multiple Rust modules.
The serial actor still failed to finish main.rs, CLI glue, build/install, and integrated verification before cancellation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial failure includes ordinary incomplete implementation and assembly work.
Parallel failure includes absence of the implementation artifact after child cancellation rather than a completed but incorrect program.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported comparative process difference and one realized parallel-side adverse pattern

candidates.reason: Implementation was explicitly assigned to agent-5, so the issue is a failed child and no recovery rather than no active implementation owner.
Parallel did not produce multiple component implementations needing reconciliation; the only implementation owner failed before returning code.
No complete component set or entry point was ready for assembly, and the implementation child's unfinished scope was broader than final packaging alone.
The parent managed exploration and assigned a coder for the pipeline; the observed failure was lack of takeover after that child failed, not an ownerless end-to-end pipeline.
The parallel run did not block all productive work behind one mandatory preflight oracle; it used multiple exploration children and then a separate implementation child.
Exploration was a first phase, but the downstream adverse event is the stopped implementation child with no takeover; retaining Serial Investigation would duplicate that same chain.
The implementation path started late, but the directly evidenced boundary is the failed implementation child and missing takeover, not a separate starvation allocation.
Five exploration children completed and returned reports; there is no independent collective fan-out exhaustion episode beyond the later failed implementation child.
The implementation assignment was broad, but the observed adverse state is that the child was stopped and no one took over; oversized scope would duplicate the same cancellation chain.

The exploration children received detailed area briefs and the implementation child was directed to read all reports; no already-known required fact is shown absent from the relevant brief and causing unusable work.
No separately implemented components from different children reached an incompatible integration point, so there is no missing cross-agent interface contract to classify.
The returned exploration reports were available to the parent and implementation child; no specific known fact is shown lost in transfer and then repeated or omitted.
The reports were substantial, but the implementer was stopped before completion; there is no direct evidence that report bulk rather than cancellation made the handoff unusable.
No receiver is shown acting on a superseded report or workspace state; the stale shared todo observations did not become a stale implementation handoff.
The five reports did not present unresolved incompatible contracts that blocked integration; the implementation child was stopped before producing a conflict to adjudicate.

The parent did not make an observable whole-task acceptance decision after receiving a candidate; closure came through cancellation and artifact collection, and evaluator failure alone cannot establish this label.
There was no replacement or retry child that repeated prior work without inherited checkpoints; the implementation child was a first attempt after exploration.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The child stop is visible, but it is the same chain as the retained recovery failure; the selected corrective boundary is taking over or reassigning after the child failed.
No complete or mutually compatible implementation candidate existed for promotion; reports and unfinished child work are not a directly packageable solution.
No child implementation was merged after an integrated verification pass, and no post-merge verification issue is evidenced.
The delegated implementation was not completed or retrievable, so the problem is not a missed join of available implementation work.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; exploration findings were returned to the parent.

The parent delegated the required implementation to agent-5; that child then failed because it was stopped before finishing, and the parent did not resume, reassign, or implement the missing scope before closure.
candidates.realized_consequence: Required implementation work was abandoned after child failure, leaving the parallel submission without a buildable reimplementation.
candidates.near_match_reason: The cancellation is observable, but the retained issue is the unrecovered failed child result; labeling the termination separately would double-count one lifecycle chain.

candidates.reason: The completed exploration results were returned and the parent used them as input to the implementation-child brief; there is no completed result ignored at a decision point.
The parent waited on a delegated implementation child, but the direct observable boundary is the child failure and absence of takeover, not ignored available progress during waiting.
The children wrote separate research reports, not competing implementation files with overlapping behavior requiring reconciliation.
No live agents are shown editing the same source or configuration file and reconciling concurrent changes.
No non-entry source module produced or owned by one agent was replaced by another; the run had report writes rather than source overwrites.
No required deliverable or entry-point source was overwritten by another live agent; the original executable remained an input/artifact, not a produced clone.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing another agent's final-tree work.
Shared todo overwrites are visible, but they did not create a concrete implementation-state or final-artifact provenance problem beyond the retained failed-child chain.
Although children created temporary fixtures and reports, no generated artifact from one actor is shown contaminating another actor's verification or final implementation as a stable input.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel parent assigned the required implementation to a child, the child was stopped before finishing, and the parent did not resume, reassign, or take over before the run closed.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parallel submission had exploration artifacts but no buildable reimplementation after the failed implementation child was not recovered.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The cancellation evidence is part of the same lifecycle chain, but the retained correction is failure recovery after the stopped child rather than a separate termination label.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Early Child Termination, Late Finalization, Missing Implementation Join, Oversized Child Task, Critical-Path Starvation, Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Serial Investigation, and Blind Timeout Wait were reviewed as possible descriptions of the same late implementation/cancellation chain and rejected in favor of the directly evidenced No Failure Takeover boundary.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the failed-child no-takeover episode clears the paired retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The annotation retains one label for one coordination boundary and avoids duplicating downstream timeout, finalization, join, allocation, or monitoring symptoms from the same chain.
